entries.2a15bffaab4ea05f: In 2007, the company released the online reservation service HotPepper Beauty. The securities report states that it grew as an innovative service that changed the common practice of salon reservations. Before that, in 2000, it had launched Hot Pepper (now HotPepper Gourmet), an information magazine closely tied to daily life such as gourmet food, and started ISIZE Travel (now Jalan net), an online reservation service for accommodation facilities. In 2012, it also launched SALON BOARD, a cloud-based reservation management system for beauty salons.

entries.2fbaeca3c450a0c9: In October 2012, the company carried out a company split making itself a holding company, and changed its name to Recruit Holdings Co., Ltd. Through incorporation-type splits, it established Recruit Sumai Company Co., Ltd., Recruit Marketing Partners Co., Ltd., Recruit Lifestyle Co., Ltd., Recruit Technologies Co., Ltd. and others, and had existing subsidiaries succeed to some businesses. In April 2018, it divided its businesses into 3 strategic business units (SBUs) and placed a company overseeing the subsidiaries and businesses of each. In April 2021, it integrated 7 core operating and functional companies, including housing, lifestyle, career and jobs, into Recruit Co., Ltd., the SBU oversight company.

entries.50f300fc4edd59db: In October 2012, the company acquired Indeed, Inc., which operates a search site specializing in online job information. Indeed is a company founded in the United States in 2004. The securities report states that through this acquisition it entered in earnest the HR Technology Business, which transforms personnel-related businesses with digital technology. In June 2018, it also acquired Glassdoor, Inc. (now Glassdoor LLC, founded in the United States in 2007), which operates a site carrying job information and user-posted company reviews.
entries.5261d05eded7c791: In 1996, the company started online job information sites such as RB on the NET (now Rikunabi) and Digital B-ing (now Rikunabi NEXT). The securities report states that in the 1990s it shifted paper information magazines to the internet and then to mobile.

entries.62b6aaa46812b23c: In July 2010, the company acquired The CSI Companies, Inc., a U.S. staffing company. The securities report states that through this it introduced unit management and began the global expansion of the staffing business through M&A. In 2004, it had expanded Zexy and other marriage-related information magazines into China but withdrew after several years, and the securities report explains that this experience was used in its subsequent overseas business strategy through M&A. It then acquired Staffmark Group, LLC in the United States (October) and Advantage Resourcing Europe B.V. in Europe (December) in 2011, and Peoplebank Australia Ltd (January) and Chandler Macleod Group Limited (April) in Australia in 2015.
entries.62e08d76e8c06536: In March 1960, Daigaku Shimbun Kokokusha was founded in Minato Ward, Tokyo, with the aim of placing companies' job advertisements in university newspapers. It then concluded contracts to handle advertisements for multiple university newspapers on an exclusive basis, and in October 1960 established Daigaku Kokoku Co., Ltd. as a corporate organization. In April 1963, it changed its name to Nihon Recruitment Center Co., Ltd., and in August of the same year the company was established as Nihon Recruit Center Co., Ltd. In April 1984, it changed its name to Recruit Co., Ltd.

entries.9496ba61fdd82d38: A business that operates websites connecting users with shops and companies in fields such as beauty, travel, dining and housing, mainly in Japan. In the fiscal year ended March 2026, it changed its name from the Matching & Solutions Business to its current name. Representative services include HotPepper Beauty for beauty, Jalan for travel, HotPepper Gourmet for dining and SUUMO for housing, combined with SaaS (software used over the internet) that helps shops with their work, such as the 13 Air Business Tools, including the payment app Air Pay and the POS register app Air Regi. Fees, in many fields, follow an “Expected Action Volume Plan” based on the number of user actions expected on the site and the cost of acquiring them, and in the beauty field, since January 2026 it has also introduced a “GMV-linked model” under which it receives consideration according to the total value of transactions generated via the site. Revenue from external customers for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥563,584 million, the smallest of the three [[term:segment|segments]], while EBITDA+S was ¥154,976 million (¥154.9 billion, up 13.0% year on year), larger than the Staffing Business, and the EBITDA+S margin was 27.4%. The number of employees was 14,096 as of March 31, 2026.

entries.a26cb2fd94a1712f: This is the HR technology business in Japan, which includes Indeed as well as Rikunabi NEXT, a job-change site, and Recruit Agent, a recruitment service. On April 1, 2025, the human resources field that had previously been in the Matching and Solutions business was moved here. In Japan, through a job distribution mechanism called Indeed PLUS, companies' job postings are automatically distributed to job boards such as Rikunabi NEXT and Townwork, and the annual securities report states that it reaches up to approximately 7-tenths of the users of major job sites in Japan. entries.ae6acaccba644486: A business that dispatches people for roles such as clerical work, manufacturing and light work, and various specialized occupations, to companies. Dispatch staff are recruited and registered in advance, and Group companies select people who match the wishes of client companies, sign employment contracts with them, and then dispatch them. The [[term:annual-securities-report|annual securities report]] states that a distinguishing feature of this business is that it does not end at placement: dispatch fees, including the wages of dispatch staff, continue to be recorded as revenue while the staff are working, and that because dispatch staff tend to want to work near their homes, “local matching,” with sales bases in each region, is important. Revenue from external customers for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥1,679,327 million, the largest of the 3 [[term:segment|segments]]. However, EBITDA+S (operating income with depreciation and amortization, share-based compensation expenses and other items added back), which the annual securities report uses as segment profit, was ¥99,744 million (¥99.7 billion), the smallest of the 3, and the EBITDA+S margin on revenue was 5.9%. The fact that revenue includes dispatch staff wages is a premise to keep in mind when comparing the size of revenue with the low margin. It had 13,354 employees as of March 31, 2026.
entries.b2e85c05ec28bc34: A temporary staffing business in Europe, the United States and Australia, which began with the acquisition of the U.S. company The CSI Companies, Inc. in 2010 and has expanded through M&A. In Europe, the company provides staffing services under brands such as Start People, Unique, USG Professionals, Secretary Plus, Bright Plus and Solvus; in the United States, under brands such as Staffmark and CSI Companies; and in Australia, under brands such as Chandler Macleod and Peoplebank. Revenue for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥856,551 million (¥856.5 billion), down 0.6% year on year.

entries.b7acc4b188a0732f: A business that connects job seekers and companies offering jobs, centered on the online job matching and recruitment platform “Indeed.” Indeed has the mission “We help people get jobs” and, according to the annual securities report, holds profiles of more than 665 million job seekers and is the world’s largest job information site, used by 3.5 million corporate clients a year (based on comScore visit figures for March 2026). Companies can post job advertisements, view candidate profiles and arrange interviews, and pay fees either on a pay-for-performance model or a subscription model. Also included in this business are “Glassdoor,” which carries job information and user-posted company reviews; the Japanese job-change site “Rikunabi NEXT”; and the placement service “Recruit Agent.” Revenue from external customers for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥1,454,440 million, the 2nd-largest of the 3 [[term:segment|segments]], but EBITDA+S, the segment profit, was ¥549,995 million (¥549.9 billion, up 21.5% year on year), the largest of the 3, and the EBITDA+S margin was 37.7%. The company cites progress in efficiency, including a decrease in personnel costs, as the reason. The number of employees was 18,005 as of March 31, 2026, the largest of the 3 businesses.
